A small island off Dakar, reached by the Portuguese in 1444 and held in turn by the Dutch, English and French, who made it a base for trade, including in slaves.

Its House of Slaves, built in the late 18th century, with its Door of No Return facing the sea, became a place of pilgrimage for the African diaspora and visiting leaders, among them Nelson Mandela, Pope John Paul II and Barack Obama. Historians argue that far fewer captives left from Goree than from ports such as Ouidah, but it stands for the whole Atlantic slave trade. It was one of the first UNESCO World Heritage Sites, in 1978. Its people were among the citizens of the Four Communes.
